rationale: An asynchronous invocation that keeps failing is retried twice by Lambda and then dropped, unless the function has an on-failure destination or a dead letter queue to send it to. The event is gone at that point: whatever S3 notification, EventBridge rule or SNS message triggered the work leaves no record that the work never happened, so a function that is failing for everything it receives looks the same from the outside as one with nothing to do. That matters for any function on a security path - a remediation, a log shipper, a quarantine action - where the missing invocation is the incident.
remediation: Configure an on-failure destination on the function's asynchronous invocation configuration, pointing at an SQS queue, an SNS topic or an EventBridge bus, or set a dead letter queue on the function
